definitions.gloss: to run into difficulties; to make slow progress; to be stalled
definitions.explanation: To encounter obstacles that slow or halt progress. Originally a nautical term meaning rough sailing, now widely used for negotiations, projects, and any process that hits snags.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}が{難航|なんこう}している。
{人手不足|ひとでぶそく}で{工事|こうじ}が{難航|なんこう}している。
examples.english: The construction is having difficulties due to a labor shortage.

examples.japanese: {与野党|よやとう}の{意見|いけん}が{対立|たいりつ}して、{法案|ほうあん}の{審議|しんぎ}が{難航|なんこう}を{極|きわ}めている。
examples.english: With the ruling and opposition parties at odds, deliberation on the bill is facing extreme difficulties.

notes:
Originally a nautical term — {難|なん} (difficulty) + {航|こう} (voyage) — meaning a rough sea crossing. Now used almost exclusively in the figurative sense of any process encountering serious obstacles.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {交渉|こうしょう}が{難航|なんこう}する — negotiations hit difficulties
- {審議|しんぎ}が{難航|なんこう}する — deliberations stall
- {調整|ちょうせい}が{難航|なんこう}する — coordination runs into trouble
- {難航|なんこう}を{極|きわ}める — to face extreme difficulties
- {難航|なんこう}が{予想|よそう}される — difficulties are expected

USAGE:
Very common in news reporting, especially about political negotiations, business deals, and large projects. The noun form {難航|なんこう} is also used without する: {難航|なんこう}が{続|つづ}く (difficulties continue).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {行|い}き{詰|づ}まる — to reach a deadlock (more complete stoppage)
- {苦戦|くせん}する — to struggle, fight an uphill battle (more about effort)
- {停滞|ていたい}する — to stagnate (emphasizes lack of movement)
